title: Plate with a hole in tension (Kirsch)
description: Steel plate 200 x 200 x 2 mm with a 10 mm hole in the middle (width 20 x the hole diameter), pulled with 100 MPa on the gross section. Quarter model 100 x 100 x 1 mm minus the hole: x = 0 and y = 0 are symmetry planes and z = 0 is the mid-plane, all three sliding supports. The pull (-100 MPa pressure) is on the end x = 100. Plate length, thickness and load are not part of Kirsch's solution: Kt does not depend on them in a thin plate, so they were chosen here.

quantities.label: x stress at the hole edge across the load, (0, 5, 0)
quantities.formula: s (1 - 2 cos 2 theta) at theta = 90 deg, s = remote stress
quantities.citation: Kirsch 1898; Timoshenko & Goodier, Theory of Elasticity, 3rd ed., McGraw-Hill 1970, Section 35, section to be checked
quantities.tolerance_reason: The finite width (d/W = 1/20) raises Kt by a few tenths of a percent, and CalculiX extrapolates the stress from the integration points to the hole surface (up to about 1 %); the band covers both plus the mesh.

quantities.label: Peak von Mises stress away from singularities (the hole edge is not one)
quantities.formula: s (1 - 2 cos 2 theta) at theta = 90 deg; the stress there is uniaxial, so von Mises = s_theta
